notes: Track A selection anchored on NYT/Sunday Times list placement and major prizes; Track B on reported unit sales and chart placement.

Several Tier-1 sales confirmations use Wikipedia as a secondary aggregation of list placements rather than the NYT list archive directly. Flagged per record; upgrade to primary archive on a later pass.

Track B titles carry systematically less professional review coverage than Track A. This is a real property of the market, not a research gap — commercial and author-native titles are documented through trade press and sales data rather than criticism. Driver counts for Track B are correspondingly lower.
Reception evidence for Track A drawn largely from Lit Hub's Book Marks review aggregator, which reproduces attributed verbatim excerpts; the originating outlet is named in every `source` field.
dropped: Trust (Hernan Diaz, 2022) — co-winner of the 2023 Pulitzer, dropped for this pass because no aggregated review page resolved; candidate for a later pass.
A Promised Land (Obama, 2020) — the period's biggest seller, but nonfiction and outside the declared fiction scope.
